```{r,echo=FALSE}
nAnB_target = sample(2:6,1)
nA_and_nB = sample((nAnB_target+1):10,2)
nA = nA_and_nB[1]
nB = nA_and_nB[2]
while(T){
    A = sample(letters,nA)
    B = sample(letters,nB)
    AuB = unique(c(A,B))
    AnB = character()
    for(i in A){
        if(i %in% B){
            AnB = c(AnB,i)
        }
    }
    AuB = sample(AuB)
    AnB = sample(AnB)
    nAuB = length(AuB)
    nAnB = length(AnB)
    if(nAnB==nAnB_target){break}
}
ach = 0:26

al = paste0("* ",ach,collapse="\n")
sol1 = paste0(1*(nA==ach),collapse="")
sol2 = paste0(1*(nB==ach),collapse="")
sol3 = paste0(1*(nAnB==ach),collapse="")
sol4 = paste0(1*(nAuB==ach),collapse="")

```

Question
========

Let set $A$ and set $B$ represent collections of lower-case letters:

$$A=\{`r paste0(A,collapse=",\\,")`\}$$
$$B=\{`r paste0(B,collapse=",\\,")`\}$$

Calculate the following [cardinalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinality):

* $n(A)=$ ##ANSWER1##
* $n(B)=$ ##ANSWER2##
* $n(A\cap B)=$ ##ANSWER3##
* $n(A\cup B)=$ ##ANSWER4##

Answerlist
--------

`r al`
`r al`
`r al`
`r al`

Solution
========

Set $A$ has `r nA` elements. $$n(A)=`r nA`$$

Set $B$ has `r nB` elements. $$n(B)=`r nB`$$

Next, identify the intersection. What elements are common to both sets?

$$A\cap B ~=~ \{`r paste0(AnB,collapse=",\\,")`\}$$


Set $A\cap B$ has `r nAnB` elements. $$n(A\cap B)=`r nAnB`$$

Next, you could try writing out all elements of the union.

$$A\cup B ~=~ \{`r paste0(AuB,collapse=",\\,")`\}$$

However, it is probably easier to use the [inclusion-exclusion principle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inclusion%E2%80%93exclusion_principle):

$$n(A\cup B)~=~n(A)+n(B)-n(A\cap B)$$
$$n(A\cup B)~=~`r nA`+`r nB`-`r nAnB`$$
$$n(A\cup B)~=~`r nAuB`$$
